The comparator contract itself must be redesigned.

blocks.text: Stability is a property of the sorting operation, not of the business-key comparator itself. When the library contract guarantees it, equal-key records retain encounter order. Decorating with originalIndex makes the same requirement explicit and works even with an otherwise unstable sort. Merely hoping for stability is not a contract, and reversing equal blocks intentionally violates the required relative order.

blocks.text: Comparison count and comparison cost multiply: Θ(n log n) comparisons × Θ(m) work per comparison = Θ(m n log n), matching the offered O(m n log n) bound. Recomputing two keys changes only a constant factor.

O(n log n) hides the length-m work inside every comparison. O(n + m) adds independent terms instead of multiplying per-comparison cost. O(n²m) is a looser upper bound, not the tightest offered bound. Precomputing keys could change the accounting, but the prompt explicitly excludes caching.
